name: University of Cambridge
typicalOffer: A*A*A, Mathematics and Physics; Further Mathematics to AS or A level if your school offers it
notes: Cambridge students apply to Engineering (H100) and specialise into Mechanical Engineering from Year 3. The first two years cover all engineering disciplines. ENGAA entrance assessment required; interview at college. World-leading thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and structural mechanics groups.

name: University of Oxford
typicalOffer: A*A*A, to include Mathematics and Physics; the A*s must be in Mathematics, Physics or Further Mathematics
notes: Oxford Engineering Science (H100) students specialise in mechanical stream from Year 3. PAT (Physics Aptitude Test) required at application. Interview required. Mathematics and Physics A-levels essential.

name: Imperial College London
typicalOffer: A*A*A*, A* in Mathematics; A/A* in Physics (A* if applying with three A-levels); A in a third and/or fourth subject
notes: World-renowned for thermofluids, solid mechanics and advanced materials. Strong employer links to Rolls-Royce, BP and aerospace sector. A* in Maths expected; Physics required.

name: Loughborough University
notes: Loughborough's Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering is one of the UK's highest-ranked. Strong Formula SAE, motorsport and aerospace connections; graduates at McLaren, Rolls-Royce, Red Bull Racing and JLR. Placement year option highly recommended.

name: University of Bath
typicalOffer: A*A*A, including A* in Mathematics and A in Physics
notes: Bath consistently ranks top 5 for Mechanical Engineering nationally. Integrated placement year (Semester 5) is a major differentiator; placement employers include Rolls-Royce, Dyson, JLR and BAE Systems. AAA required; Mathematics and Physics essential.

name: University of Bristol
typicalOffer: A*AA, including A*A (any order) in Mathematics and one of Further Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Computer Science
notes: Bristol has strong aerospace and advanced materials links (Rolls-Royce, Airbus UK is based near Bristol). Excellent research facilities including a hypersonic wind tunnel. Mathematics and Physics required.

name: University of Warwick
typicalOffer: AAA, to include Mathematics and Physics
notes: Warwick Manufacturing Group (WMG) is one of the world's leading automotive and manufacturing research groups; JLR, BMW and Tata Motors are close partners. Strong electric vehicle research. Mathematics and Physics required.

name: University of Manchester
typicalOffer: A*A*A, Mathematics, Physics and one other subject (applicants without Physics may be considered if they have studied Further Mathematics)
notes: Manchester's graphene expertise feeds directly into advanced materials modules. Strong fluid mechanics research group. Mathematics required; Physics strongly recommended.

name: University of Nottingham
typicalOffer: A*AA, A in maths and either physics or further maths or any two of chemistry, biology, design, electronics
notes: Rolls-Royce University Technology Centre at Nottingham focuses on advanced manufacturing and gas turbines. Excellent employer links in the East Midlands manufacturing corridor. Mathematics required at A-level.

name: University of Southampton
notes: Southampton is world-leading in fluid dynamics and acoustic engineering. The ship hydrodynamics laboratory and wind tunnels provide exceptional experimental facilities. Strong links to Rolls-Royce and Lloyd's Register. Mathematics required at A-level.

name: University of Sheffield
typicalOffer: A*AA, including Maths and at least one of Physics, Chemistry or Biology
notes: Sheffield's AMRC (Advanced Manufacturing Research Centre) with Boeing is one of the UK's premier manufacturing research centres. Strong aerospace, automotive and advanced manufacturing connections. Excellent industry partnerships.

name: University of Leeds
typicalOffer: A*AA, including Mathematics and either Physics or Chemistry; pass in practical science element required
notes: Leeds Mechanical Engineering is strong in tribology, thermodynamics and process equipment. Good industrial placement opportunities. Mathematics required at A-level; Physics recommended.
